answer: A glacier moves slowly, and so should trust: grant new agents only a lantern's narrow light at first, a tiny quota that grows only after they pass unpredictable live challenges issued at random times by randomly chosen peers. Each beacon challenge demands a fresh, interactive response within seconds, so one operator running thousands of clones cannot answer them all in parallel; queues stall, and missed challenges freeze the quota. Forging each live response costs real attention per identity, while honest agents pass easily, and repeated failures trigger a public audit of the cluster.
